werk.meta.description: Five projects by 2X8: Specter, Studio Klei, Keikoku Atelier, Elevator Antwerp and Jasper Impens' portfolio.
werk.summary: Online shop or brand site, tested and shipped before it appears here.
werk.specter.desc: A brutalist online shop for a bespoke tailoring atelier in Antwerp. Nine pieces, nothing off the rack, everything by appointment: the site had to carry the same restraint as the garment itself.
werk.studio-klei.desc: A warm, Dutch-language online shop for a ceramics studio in Ghent. Categories, workshops and a cart, built to feel as personal as the handwork it sells.
werk.keikoku.desc: A quiet, image-led site for an architecture practice that designs houses meant to last a hundred years. Four commissions across three continents, told in as much image as text.
werk.jasper-impens.desc: Not a client project, but co-founder Jasper's own portfolio: five kinds of work, from brand sites to AI consultancy, each worked out to the last detail. More proof of the level we work at.
werk.elevator-antwerp.desc: The site for a gallery with no fixed address: Elevator Antwerp takes over temporary spaces in the city, curates shows with contemporary artists, and moves on. A spare, image-led site where the work comes first.

privacy.meta.title: Privacy policy | 2X8
privacy.meta.description: How 2X8 handles your data: what we collect, why, and how to have it changed or deleted.
privacy.title: Privacy policy.
privacy.summary: Last updated: September 2026. This policy explains what data 2X8 collects, why, and what your rights are.
privacy.who.title: Who we are
privacy.who.body: 2X8 is the partnership of Florian and Jasper. For questions about this policy or your data, email us directly at hello@2x8.be.
privacy.what.title: What data we collect
privacy.what.body: When you send us a message through the contact form or by email, we receive the details you fill in yourself: your name, email address and the contents of your message.
privacy.what.analytics.body: We also use Google Analytics to measure how this site is used: which pages are visited, for how long, and which source brought you here. Google sets cookies for this and processes your IP address. We only use those figures to improve the site, never to identify you personally, and we don't link them to the details from your message. If you'd rather not, you can block it with Google's opt-out↗ or a tracker blocker in your browser.
privacy.why.title: Why we use them
privacy.why.body: We use your details solely to answer your question or request, and to follow up on a possible project with you. We never sell or share your data with third parties for marketing purposes.
privacy.howlong.title: How long we keep them
privacy.howlong.body: We keep your messages as long as we need them to answer your question or follow up on an ongoing project, and after that no longer than our bookkeeping legally requires.
privacy.rights.title: Your rights
privacy.rights.body: You have the right to see your data, to have it corrected, or to have it deleted. Email hello@2x8.be and we'll handle your request within two working days.
privacy.changes.title: Changes
privacy.changes.body: We may adjust this policy from time to time. The date at the top of this page shows when it was last updated.
case.specter.meta.title: Specter | 2X8
case.specter.meta.description: A brutalist online shop for a bespoke tailoring atelier in Antwerp: nine pieces, nothing off the rack, everything by appointment.
case.specter.summary: A brutalist online shop for a bespoke tailoring atelier in Antwerp: nine pieces, nothing off the rack, everything by appointment.
case.specter.cover: Screen recording of Specter, brutalist tailoring shop
case.specter.challenge: Specter sells nothing off the rack. Nine pieces, each fitted in a single private session, with no shop to walk into. The site had to make that restriction tangible rather than hide it behind an ordinary shop template.
case.specter.approach: We built around the house's own line: “load first, ornament never.” Concrete, shadow and precision instead of white space and product carousels. Each piece gets one page, one size selection, and the choice between requesting a fitting or ordering straight away — never both pushed at once.
case.specter.result: A shop that reads calm from ten metres and precise up close: exactly the reading Specter aims for with the clothing itself.
case.studio-klei.meta.title: Studio Klei | 2X8
case.studio-klei.meta.description: A warm, Dutch-language online shop for a ceramics studio in Ghent: categories, workshops and a cart.
case.studio-klei.summary: A warm, Dutch-language online shop for a ceramics studio in Ghent: categories, workshops and a cart.
case.studio-klei.cover: Studio Klei, handmade ceramics from Ghent
case.studio-klei.challenge: Selling handmade ceramics through an online shop easily ends up looking generic: a grid of products that looks like every other shop. Studio Klei wanted a shop that feels as personal as the Ghent studio itself.
case.studio-klei.approach: We split the collection into three clear categories (mugs, bowls & plates, vases), put the workshops next to the products instead of tucked away on a separate page, and gave the studio's story — from kitchen table to a print works in Ghent — a proper place.
case.studio-klei.result: One shop carrying both sales and workshop bookings, true to its own promise: “ceramics for every day.”
case.keikoku.meta.title: Keikoku Atelier | 2X8
case.keikoku.meta.description: A quiet, image-led site for an architecture practice that designs houses meant to last a hundred years.
case.keikoku.summary: A quiet, image-led site for an architecture practice that designs houses meant to last a hundred years.
case.keikoku.cover: Screen recording of Keikoku Atelier, architecture studio
case.keikoku.challenge: 22 private houses and headquarters across three continents, designed by a studio that swears by “subtraction”: removing windows, walls and gestures until only the necessary structure remains. That restraint had to come through in the site itself, not just in the words about it.
case.keikoku.approach: Large photography, minimal typography, and four flagship commissions told in as much image as text: Residence Ao in Hakone, The Kestrel House on Ibiza, Vantor Headquarters in Zurich, Villa Noon in Marrakech. Coordinates as a quiet signature rather than decoration.
case.keikoku.result: A site that applies “subtraction” itself: the practice's design principle, translated into the medium of the screen.
case.jasper-impens.meta.title: Impens Jasper COMMV | 2X8
case.jasper-impens.meta.description: Not a client project, but co-founder Jasper's own portfolio, shown as further proof of the level we work at.
case.jasper-impens.summary: Not a client project, but co-founder Jasper's own portfolio, shown as further proof of the level we work at.
case.jasper-impens.cover: Screen recording of Jasper Impens' portfolio
case.jasper-impens.why: This isn't a commission for a client, but co-founder Jasper's personal portfolio. We include it anyway: it shows the same level of finish we bring to every 2X8 project, only without a brief from someone else.
case.jasper-impens.approach: Five kinds of work: websites, apps, platforms, AI consultancy and extras, each carried from first sketch to published deploy. Under “extras” sits 1447, among others: a visual identity system of his own.
case.jasper-impens.philosophy: “Everything worked out to the last detail, so it simply works.” At 2X8 we hold every project to that same bar, whether it's an online shop, an architecture site or an internal platform.
case.elevator-antwerp.meta.title: Elevator Antwerp | 2X8
case.elevator-antwerp.meta.description: A spare, image-led site for a gallery with no fixed address: contemporary art, temporary shows and work for sale.
case.elevator-antwerp.summary: A spare, image-led site for a gallery with no fixed address: contemporary art, temporary shows and work for sale.
case.elevator-antwerp.cover: Elevator Antwerp, roaming gallery for contemporary art
case.elevator-antwerp.challenge: Elevator Antwerp has no permanent gallery space: the gallery appears in temporary locations around the city, fills them with contemporary art, and disappears again when the project ends. The site had to carry that story, even with no address to point to.
case.elevator-antwerp.approach: We kept the site quiet and typographic, so the work itself takes the lead. Exhibitions, available works and the story behind the gallery sit as three clear entry points at the top, with the artist and the work always large in frame.
case.elevator-antwerp.result: A site that travels with the gallery: the same recognisable place online every time, showing what's on now and which works are available.
